sources.title: Lectures on the Poisson Process
sources.version: Author-hosted version dated 21 August 2017; prepublication text for the IMS Textbook published by Cambridge University Press in 2017.
sources.authority: Günter Last, Institute of Stochastics, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology; coauthor Mathew Penrose, University of Bath; PDF hosted on KIT author/institute site.
sources.access: Public author/institution-hosted PDF; title page says commercial reproduction is prohibited. Kept in the private source cache and paraphrased in the dossier; no text is reproduced.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 1, printed pp. 1-8: Poisson distributions, thinning/superposition relations and Poisson approximations (Propositions 1.1-1.5).
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Selected proposition proofs read in full; other chapters remain unread.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 2, printed pp. 9-18: point processes as random counting measures, proper/local-finiteness notions, intensity/Campbell formula and Laplace functional law criterion.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Proposition 2.7 Campbell formula and Proposition 2.10 equivalence of distribution/Laplace-functional descriptions, including proof, read.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 3, printed pp. 19-25: Poisson process definition, superposition, existence and mixed-binomial construction.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Theorem 3.6 existence and Theorem 3.9 Laplace functional proof read.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 4, printed pp. 26-37: Mecke identity/converse, factorial moment measures and Janossy measures.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Theorem 4.1 Mecke equation and proof, including the converse characterization, read; equations on factorial moments and Janossy measures read.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 8, printed pp. 69-81: stationary point processes, finite intensity, second factorial moment/reduced measure, mixing and spatial mean ergodic result.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Theorem 8.14 proves L1 convergence for dilations of compact convex windows under stationarity and finite intensity; it does not state a rate or CLT. The proof is long and was read in full.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 9, printed pp. 82-91: refined Campbell formula, Palm distributions and Poisson Mecke-Slivnyak property.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Theorem 9.1 refined Campbell and Theorem 9.4 Slivnyak proofs read. Theorem 9.1 uses Proposition 8.7 (read in Chapter 8) and Proposition 6.3; Chapter 6 Section 6.1 / Proposition 6.3 (PDF pp. 57-60) were read to close that measurability route.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 13, printed pp. 127-135: random measures, Cox-process definition and conditional laws/moments.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Proposition 13.6 variance decomposition and Theorem 13.8 Cox-Mecke characterization were read with proofs. Theorem 13.7 states directing-measure law identification and its in-section proof route was read, but the final uniqueness step invokes Proposition B.5; Appendix B.1 p. 275 was also read and B.5 itself cites external reference [78] for analyticity/uniqueness. Thus Theorem 13.7 is not counted as a complete proof source here.

actual_reading.sections: Appendix B.1 Proposition B.5 on uniqueness from Laplace transforms and Appendix B.2 Theorem B.11 mean ergodic theorem, including its full proof.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Theorem B.11 proof on pp. 277-278 supports the input invoked by Chapter 8 Theorem 8.14. Proposition B.5 is only stated on p. 275; its proof of Laplace-transform uniqueness cites external reference [78], so it does not close the final uniqueness step in Chapter 13 Theorem 13.7.

actual_reading.sections: Chapter 6 Section 6.1 (Borel spaces), read to verify a measurability input used by the refined Campbell theorem.
actual_reading.proof_anchors_and_gaps: Definition 6.1 and Propositions 6.2-6.3, including the measurable enumeration of finite and locally finite counting measures and the proof of Proposition 6.3, read. This closes the Chapter 9 Theorem 9.1 proof dependency on Proposition 6.3. Other Chapter 6 results remain unread; in particular Chapter 13 Theorem 13.11 invokes Proposition 6.9 and Theorem 6.11, which are not used as dependencies.

sources.unread_scope: All portions outside the chapter ranges above and Appendix B.1-B.2 (PDF pp. 274-278), including the rest of Chapter 6 (except Section 6.1, pp. 57-60), most of Chapters 5-7 and 10-22, and Appendices A and B.3 onward, were not read. In particular Chapter 13 Theorem 13.11 invokes unread Proposition 6.9 and Theorem 6.11. Extracting the complete 305-page PDF does not count as reading those portions.
